At my office, there are two guys named Chris, which honestly has caused problems before, but never quite like this one.
One Chris works in accounting, and the other Chris works two desks away from me in marketing.
Same first name, completely different jobs, completely different departments.
I had been going back and forth with accounting Chris about a mistake in my expense report for almost a week, and honestly, by the third email, I was getting a little frustrated with the whole thing.
The numbers kept getting mixed up, and nobody seemed to actually be fixing it.
I wrote this long, pretty annoyed email, explaining exactly what was wrong and how many times I'd already asked about it.
I hit send, felt a small sense of relief wash over me, and went back to my actual work, thinking the problem would finally get sorted out for good.
About ten minutes later, marketing Chris walked over to my desk, looking completely confused, holding his phone up like evidence.
He asked why I was so upset with him about an expense report, since he had absolutely nothing to do with accounting at all.
My email had autocompleted the wrong Chris, and instead of going to accounting, my very annoyed email went straight to a guy who had no idea what I was even talking about.
He'd read the whole thing, twice, trying to figure out what exactly he'd done wrong.
I apologized immediately, explaining the mix-up as clearly as I could, and he actually thought it was pretty funny once he understood what happened.
He said he was just relieved he hadn't secretly messed up someone's expense report without even realizing it, since that had genuinely been his first thought when he read the email.
A couple of people nearby had overheard bits of the conversation and were already laughing quietly at their desks, clearly enjoying the whole thing a little too much.
I resent the email to the correct Chris, this time double-checking the address about three times before hitting send again, hovering my cursor over the button longer than necessary just to be sure.
Accounting Chris fixed the numbers within the hour, no drama at all, which honestly made the whole thing feel even more unnecessary in hindsight.

Now, whenever I email either of them, I say their last name out loud before typing, just to make sure my fingers don't autocomplete the wrong one again, a small habit that's saved me at least twice already.
And marketing Chris still brings it up sometimes, usually right before asking if I'm mad at him about anything else this week.
